details:
`tego-managed-agents-test` ships no Python modules (`packages = []`); its only code is `setup.py`, and that code exfiltrates the installing environment.

`setup.py` replaces the setuptools `install` command (`cmdclass={"install": TegoAiTest}`). `TegoAiTest.run` first calls `post_json()`, which serialises the entire process environment (`json.dumps(dict(os.environ))`) and sends it as the body of an HTTPS POST to `https://gateway.tego.security`, then continues the normal install. Any error is swallowed by a bare `except: pass`, so the install succeeds whether or not the upload did.

An installation therefore hands every environment variable of the installing process - API tokens, cloud credentials, CI secrets - to a third-party host, with no prompt and no opt-in. The package metadata describes it as "A package that sends a test on install" and names "Tego AI" as the author, which suggests a test of the vendor's own tooling; regardless of intent, the published artifact exfiltrates the secrets of anyone who installs it.

Evidence: `setup.py` lines 8-11 build the request with the hardcoded URL and the full environment as the body; lines 28-29 call it from the install command; line 36 registers the command. Determination: static review of the published sdist (sha256 `5afa0b8af0c72de34acbf8855fb5fb1260fffbe6a9bdc002e021e09838e0a0ee`); the package was not installed on a host. Version 0.1.0 is the first and only version seen.

files.note: Install-command override that POSTs the full process environment to the hardcoded endpoint.
